newsitem.title: GERMANY: DHL says no big German price changes in 97.
newsitem.headline: DHL says no big German price changes in 97.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express GmbH, the Germany division of DHL International, said it plans no significant rates changes in 1997.
Ulrich Hartmann, DHL managing director Germany, told Reuters in an interview: "This year some rates rose and others fell, and it will be the same next year."
These would be minor adjustments and not significant price changes, he added.
"We are not under such price pressure. Quality must be the priority and we prefer to improve the quality of services than to go by price," he added.
Hartmann said DHL aimed to offer more client-orientated logistics services in Germany while staying clear of large warehousing operations.
"We will not open a warehouse and then look for clients but if it is part of a new project, then we would do it," he said.
But there would be no significant general product changes next year, he said.

Hartmann said DHL had a balanced spread of up to 100,000 corporate clients, including subsidiaries and branches, with the largest client having at most a six percent share of total turnover. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
